summary:
Moon & Mars Detectives is an interactive educational game created by Eric and Valentín, two seven-year-old first-grade students from Colegio Miguel de Cervantes in Uruguay.

Our project brings the stories of NASA's equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars to life through puzzles, mini-games, and interactive scientific challenges.

Players become space detectives and explore real NASA missions, including Apollo 17, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, and Phoenix. Through interactive activities, they discover what these explorers accomplished, the scientific discoveries they made, and why their missions ended.

Our game addresses the challenge “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” by transforming the history of space exploration into an engaging learning experience for children.

With the help of ChatGPT as a programming tool, we transformed our ideas into a playable web application.

We believe that science should be accessible, exciting, and fun for everyone, especially young children.

Made by kids. For kids.
details:
Moon & Mars Detectives

What is our project?

Moon & Mars Detectives is an interactive educational game created by Eric and Valentín, two seven-year-old first-grade students from Colegio Miguel de Cervantes in Uruguay, with the support of their parents.

We wanted to create a fun way for other children to learn about the spacecraft and scientific equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars.

Our game transforms real NASA missions into an interactive adventure where players become space detectives, solve challenges, and discover the stories behind these incredible machines.

How does it work?

Players begin by learning about the Space Race and the first human missions to the Moon. They then complete puzzles to reveal historic space vehicles and unlock information about their missions. The game features five real space explorers: the Apollo 17 Lunar Rover, which helps players discover how astronauts explored the Moon and what happened to their vehicle; Sojourner, which introduces a navigation challenge where players guide a rover around obstacles and collect scientific samples; Spirit, which invites players to investigate clues about water in the Martian environment; Opportunity, which helps children understand how solar panels work and how dust storms can affect a rover's energy supply; and Phoenix, which challenges players to search for water ice beneath the Martian surface. Players also complete matching activities and a final quiz to reinforce what they have learned. Each challenge connects gameplay with real scientific discoveries and historical information from NASA.

Our project combines storytelling, science, and interactive games to make space exploration understandable and exciting for young children. Instead of simply presenting information about spacecraft left behind on the Moon and Mars, we invite players to investigate their stories through activities inspired by their real missions. One of the most special aspects of our project is that it was imagined by children for children. We believe children can create educational experiences that inspire other children to become interested in science.

The application was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It runs directly in a web browser without requiring downloads, installations, or specialized hardware. With the support of our parents, we used ChatGPT (OpenAI) as a programming assistant to transform our ideas into a functional application. The original concept, educational content, selection of missions, and ideas for the games and challenges came from us, the students. ChatGPT helped generate and implement the code, develop the interface, resolve technical problems, and translate the application into English. Scientific information and mission imagery were obtained from NASA's official resources.

Our main goal is to encourage curiosity about science and space exploration among young children. We considered the age of our intended audience, the importance of simple instructions, engaging visuals, interactive learning, and scientific accuracy. By combining games with real NASA discoveries, we hope to make scientific knowledge more accessible and enjoyable. We also want to demonstrate how creativity, family support, and technology, including artificial intelligence, can help young students transform their ideas into real educational projects.

Our message is simple: Science is for everyone, and even the youngest explorers can inspire others.
